name: Hagar
description: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs

points: Hagar was Sarai's Egyptian handmaid, from the servants Pharaoh gave in Genesis 12:16.
Sarai laid the wrong on Abram, and Abram answered, Behold, thy maid is in thy hand. He did not say my wife; he had no attachment to Hagar. His sole purpose was the seed, not multiple wives.
When Hagar conceived, her mistress was despised in her eyes. Hagar got high minded; she stopped submitting because she carried Abram's child.

Abram was fourscore and six years old, eighty six, when Hagar bare Ishmael. Ishmael was Abram's firstborn, but the covenant did not go to Ishmael; the covenant goes through the twelve tribes of Israel.

Abraham rose up early, took bread and a bottle of water, gave it to Hagar, and sent her away with the child. That is important, because the Arabs love to talk about Abraham, we are descendants of Abraham, the Abrahamic religions. Abraham gave you a bottle of water and some bread and sent you away.

note.label: Armageddon: Islam and the Armies of the East

points: Tell me, ye that desire to be under the law, the sacrifice of the weak and beggarly elements, do ye not hear the law? Abraham had two sons, one by a bondmaid, Hagar, born after the flesh, Ishmael, and one by a freewoman, Sarah, by promise. Which things are an allegory, for these are the two covenants: Hagar is the old, from mount Sinai, which gendereth to bondage, bound to offering up animals; Sarah is the new.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

points: This Agar is mount Sinai in Arabia, and answereth to Jerusalem which now is, and is in bondage with her children under temple law. But Jerusalem which is above is free, because Christ died, and is the mother of us all. Rejoice, thou barren that bearest not: Sarah.
